title: How a clock tells your ship where it is
description:
At sea, a compass gives you north but not how far east or west you are. The fix is a clock: at local noon (the sun at its highest), read a clock still set to home time. Earth turns 15 degrees an hour, so 3 hours behind home means 45 degrees west, and every minute the clock drifts puts you a quarter of a degree, about 28 km at the equator, off. The 1714 Longitude Act offered £20,000 for half a degree, a 2-minute error; on its 1761-62 trial to Jamaica, 81 days at sea, John Harrison's H4 sea watch was 5 seconds off once its known daily rate was allowed for.

Numbers checked in code (including 100,000 simulated ships). Sources: Wikipedia, John Harrison (H4 trial) and Longitude prize (the Act's thresholds).

The math behind real problems, twice a day. Subscribe and the next one finds you.

social_caption: One minute wrong on your clock puts your ship 28 km off. Here's how a clock finds longitude, and the watch that won.
facts_checked: Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours = 15 degrees an hour; 3 hours = 45 degrees; 1 minute = 0.25 degrees (verify.py)
1 degree of longitude at the equator = 111.32 km (WGS84 radius 6,378.137 km), so 1 minute of clock error = 27.8 km, said 28 (verify.py; 100,000 simulated ships)
Longitude Act 1714: GBP 20,000 for a method accurate within 30 minutes of arc = half a degree = 2 minutes of time (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longitude_prize; verify.py)

H4 trial to Jamaica, 81 days and 5 hours; found 5 seconds slow against the known longitude of Kingston (after its daily rate), an error of 1.25 minutes of longitude (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Harrison); 120 / 5 = 24 times inside the prize (verify.py)
CTA answer: home clock 9 pm at your noon = 9 hours = 135 degrees west (verify.py)

beats.say: One minute wrong puts your ship 28 kilometers off.
Your compass shows north. It can't tell you how far east you are.
So wait for the sun to peak. That's noon, right where you are.
Now check a clock still set to home time. Say it reads 3 pm.
Earth turns 15 degrees an hour. 3 hours behind home means 45 degrees west.
But that clock has to ride a rolling ship for months.
Every minute it drifts is a quarter of a degree. 28 kilometers at the equator. Britain offered 20,000 pounds for half a degree: a 2 minute error.
John Harrison's sea watch sailed to Jamaica, 81 days, and was off by 5 seconds. 24 times better than the prize asked.
So, at your noon, home says 9 pm. How far west are you?
